We evaluated the performance of the test section at a variety of charge and discharge rates. The operating conditions for each run are shown in Table 1. The discharge loop was run at a constant power for all cases. Although the heat transfer rate from the charge loop could not be controlled at a constant power, the inlet conditions were set so that the average charge rates were near the target. Cases 1-5 started from the fully charged state and cases 6-10 started at the fully discharged state. The model described above was modified to include two glycol streams and to account for gaps between parallel MPE tubes. The experimentally measured inlet temperatures and flow rates were fed into the model and the measured fluid outlet and PCC temperatures were compared to the model to validate the results. 18 This report is available at no cost from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) at www.nrel.gov/publications. We calculated a contact resistance of approximately 3×10-4 K m2 W-1, which was used to update the glycol-glycol finite difference model. The channel-channel contact resistance was not changed in the refrigerant-glycol model because we should be able to reduce this resistance in the final design by brazing the arrays together or extruding both tubes as one part. Before we compared the model to the experimental results, we examined the PCC properties, which have a large impact on the device performance.
